request.draft:
Priya Shah
Ms. Tran
Biology 9
29 October 2026

Yeast, Sugar and Time

We wanted to know whether the amount of sugar changes how fast yeast makes carbon dioxide. Our hypothesis was that more sugar would make the balloon grow faster, up to a point.

We mixed one packet of yeast with 100 mL of warm water in each of four bottles. Each bottle got 0, 5, 10 or 20 grams of sugar, and we stretched a balloon over its neck. Every five minutes for thirty minutes we measured around each balloon with a string and a ruler. We kept the water at 40 °C by standing the bottles in a tub of warm water.

After thirty minutes the balloon on the 20 gram bottle measured 31 cm around, compared with 24 cm for 10 grams and 17 cm for 5 grams. The bottle with no sugar did not change at all.

More sugar made the balloons grow faster, which supports our hypothesis. This happens because yeast breaks down sugar for energy and gives off carbon dioxide as it does. The 20 gram balloon grew only 7 cm more than the 10 gram one, so adding more sugar helped less each time. Next time we would repeat each bottle three times, because one bottle of each is not enough to be sure.
